body_markdown:
I have always shared my love for older cars, and the histories of those I’ve owned, with my son, Joe. We’ve had great times going to car shows together, and we both appreciate the skills and dedication many car owners from my generation display with their cars from the 1960s and ’70s.


In 1974, when I was 20 years old, I purchased a blue ’71 Datsun 240Z. Over the years, I shared pictures and stories of that car with Joe on a regular basis—including how sorry I was that I eventually sold it.


Joe Carzo


Joe Carzo


Well, in 2015, I pulled into my driveway and opened the garage door, and there it was: a magnificent[1972 Datsun 240Z](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/datsun/240z/1972/1972-datsun-240z-base?id=aCn1I000000DO2VSAW) almost the same color as my ’71. My son had purchased it for me as a retirement gift. It was such an unbelievable gesture from a great kid.


Joe Carzo


The car was in terrific shape, but we eventually changed the triple Weber carbs that he installed for stock carbs rebuilt by ZTherapy. We chromed the bumpers and added an original-equipment stock exhaust, installed a new radiator, new head gasket and valves, and fitted new tires.


[The car runs great](https://www.hagerty.com/media/car-profiles/240z-and-miata-the-essential-japanese-sportscars/) and looks even greater. Just about every day I drive it, I get a thumbs-up from people of all ages—younger kids who appreciate its lines and people my age who connect with their earlier days.


They don’t know how I came to own it, of course, but I do, and I can’t tell you how proud I am of this car and of my son.


Joe Carzo
